work.title: De Non Conveniendo Cum Haereticis

paragraphs.text: I. On Not Associating with Heretics.

When you noticed that all your pernicious attempts had been opposed, and found that all your schemes against the church of God had been revealed to the whole people of God, you said that we had been and still are enemies of peace, foes of unity, and adversaries even of brotherly love. If there ought to be no difference between the worshipers of God and the enemies of his religion, why did Moses, when he saw that carnal Jewish people, whose wisdom you hold, had incurred the guilt of idolatry, not only have certain of them struck down with the sword but also want his own station to be set apart? Learn that this is written as follows: And the Lord said to Moses: Say to the children of Israel, You are a stiff-necked people; see that I do not bring another plague upon you and destroy you. Now therefore put off the robes of your glory and your ornaments, and I will show you what I am going to do to you. And the children of Israel stripped off their ornaments and their robes from Mount Horeb. And Moses took the tabernacle and pitched it outside the camp, far from the camp, and it was called the tabernacle of testimony; and it came about that everyone who sought the Lord went out to the tabernacle of testimony outside the camp. And whenever Moses went out from the tabernacle, all the people stood watching, each at the door of his own tent. They watched Moses as he went, until he entered the tabernacle; and as soon as Moses had entered the tabernacle, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the door of the tabernacle, and he spoke to Moses; and all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the door of the tabernacle, and all the people stood and worshiped, each at the door of his tent. And the Lord spoke to Moses openly, face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. But his minister, the young man Joshua son of Nun, did not leave the tabernacle. By this deed it was shown that you, who sin against God, must be avoided, and that we must withdraw from you. But, you say, 'Look, although Moses had his tabernacle in another place, he still did not desert the people, but urged them to correct the ways of their errors so that God might be gracious.' Nor do those who refused to be mixed up in your sacrilege fail in these duties; for you know that you are being told that unless you correct your ways, you will perish for ever.

So, to bring what we had begun to set out to a complete proof: whenever the people murmured against God and rose up against Moses, you have read that God said to Moses and Aaron: Withdraw from the midst of this undisciplined and stubborn people, and I will destroy them. What, then, does he want us to do, except to flee from you, the undisciplined and stubborn, so that we do not perish together with you, like those who had banded together with Korah, Dathan and Abiram? Or will you deny that you are undisciplined and stubborn? Look back at your deeds done against the Lord's church, and you will find how undisciplined and stubborn you are. In Deuteronomy Moses says: You shall not make a covenant with them nor show them mercy, nor shall you give your daughters to them in marriage, nor give his daughter to your son; for he will lead your son away from me, and he will serve foreign gods, and the Lord will be angry with you in his wrath and will quickly destroy you. Since he commands this, how can we come together with you, how can we have peace with you, deniers of the only Son of God? How could we have fulfilled that will of yours? For you see that God said through Moses about the Moabites and Ammonites: You shall not greet them in peace all the days of your life, for ever. How could Arians and Christians have been together? For you hear Moses say: There shall be no adulteress among the daughters of Israel, and he warns in every place that every adulterer is to be brought out to the gate and put to death with stones: And you shall remove the wicked one from among yourselves, he says. If he says that God so loathes fleshly adultery that he ordered all adulterers to be punished, how much more must the Lord loathe your spiritual adultery—which is why you had to be fled from and still must be. We Christians could not come together with apostates, since we find that the Holy Spirit said through Moses: God will open to you his best heavenly treasure, to give rain to your land; in its season he will bless all the work of your hands; you will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow; and you will make war on many nations, but they will not overcome you; the Lord your God will make you the head and not the tail, and you will be above and not beneath, if you heed the commandment of the Lord your God, whatever I command you this day to keep and to do, and do not turn aside from any word that I command you this day, to the right or to the left. How could we agree with the Arian pseudo-bishops of your sect, when you see that we could not have been blessed unless we did not go after your idolatry, unless we loathed your heresy of the Arians, as we loathe that of all heretics, unless we judged and held you to be the same as the pagans, namely worshipers of all the demons, unless we abhorred you as we do the Jews, who are found to be without God because they denied the only Son of God? In Joshua it says: But when the people heard the sound of the trumpets, all the people shouted with a great shout, and all the walls of the city fell down all around; and all the people went up into the city, each one straight ahead against his enemies, and they seized the city and put it under the ban, and whatever was in the city, from man to woman, from young to old, down to calf and beast of burden, they slew with the edge of the sword. And Joshua said to the two young men who had spied out the land: Go into the woman's house and bring her out with all that is hers. And the two young men who had spied out the city went into the woman's house and brought out Rahab the harlot, and her father and mother and brothers and all that was hers, and all her kindred, and they led her outside the camp of Israel; and the city was burned with fire together with everything in it. And further on: Joshua kept alive Rahab the harlot and all her father's house, and she has dwelt in Israel to this day. Since, then, you see that all the inhabitants of the city of Jericho were punished with the edge of the sword and the whole city was burned, how did you think we could come together with you, a heretic, when we recognized that you and yours deserve anathema more than they did? How could we come together with the Arian pseudo-bishops of your sect, when you see that in the city where idolaters lived no one was spared alive except Rahab alone, because she believed that our Lord is almighty, and that the idolatry in which the people of Jericho trusted had been invented by human error?

How could we have come together with you, when it is written in the third book of Kingdoms that your houses must not be set foot in, nor food eaten with you, nor water accepted from you? Holy Scripture shows that this is so: And it came to pass—it says concerning that fellow apostate of yours—the word of the man of God; and further on: And he stretched out his hand toward the altar, saying, Seize him! And the king's hand, which he had stretched out against him, withered, and he could not draw it back to himself; and the altar was split, and its fat poured out from the altar, according to what the man of God had said by the word of the Lord. And the king answered and said to the man of God: Entreat the face of the Lord your God, that my hand may be restored to me. And the man of God entreated the face of the Lord, and the king's hand was restored to him and became as it was before. And the king spoke to the man of God and said: Come into the house with me and dine, and I will give you gifts. And the man of God said to the king: Not even if you gave me half your house would I go in with you, nor will I eat bread or drink water in this place; for so the Lord commanded me by his word, saying: You shall not eat bread and you shall not drink water, and you shall not return by the way by which you came. How could we have come together with you to worship God, when such heavy punishment fell upon this man of God, who had been sent by God to rebuke King Jeroboam, because he had been deceived by that man who was called a prophet? And he went away, the scripture says next about that man of God, by another road, and did not return by the road by which he had come to Bethel. And his sons came and told him all the works that the man of God had done that day in Bethel, and the words he had spoken to the king, and they turned their father's face; and their father spoke to them, saying: Which way did he go? And his sons showed him the way by which the man of God who had come from Judah had gone. And he said to his sons: Saddle the donkey for me. And they saddled it for him, and he mounted it and went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak tree, and said to him: Are you the man of God who came from Judah? And he said: I am. And he said to him: Come with me and eat bread. And he said: I cannot go back with you, nor eat bread nor drink water in this place; for so the Lord commanded me by his word, saying: You shall not eat bread there and you shall not drink water there, and you shall not return from there by the way by which you came. And he said to him: I too am a prophet, as you are, and an angel spoke to me by the word of the Lord, saying: Bring him back with you to your house, and let him eat bread and drink water. And he lied to him and brought him back, and he ate bread in his house and drank water. And it came to pass, as they sat at table, that the word of the Lord came to the false prophet who had brought him back, and he spoke to the man of God who had come from Judah, saying: Thus says the Lord: Because you have provoked the word of the Lord and have not kept the commandment that the Lord your God commanded you, but came back and ate bread and drank water in this place, of which he said to you, You shall not eat bread nor drink water, therefore your body shall not enter the tomb of your fathers. And it came to pass, after he had eaten bread and drunk water, that they saddled the donkey for him, and he turned back and went away; and a lion met him on the road and killed him, and his body was thrown down in the road, and the donkey stood beside it, and the lion stood by his body. And men of that city came and told it in the city where the old prophet lived; and when he heard it, the one who had brought him back from the road said: This is the man of God who provoked the word of the Lord. And he went and found his body thrown down in the road, and the donkey and the lion standing over the body; and the lion had not eaten his body nor sprung upon the donkey. If this was what befell him because he had eaten bread and taken a drink of water in a profane place among foreign men, what would have befallen us if, as you desired, we had struck up friendships with you, whom we know to be a heretic, whom we know to be a denier of the only Son of God; if we had poured out prayer together with you Arians; if, finally, we had allowed ourselves to celebrate everything that we priests of the Lord celebrate together with your Arian pseudo-bishops? Meanwhile, as you go back over your most bitter deeds, you ought to recognize that you were sent to deceive us just as that false prophet was sent to that man of God. For just as he, though he was a false prophet, called himself a prophet in order to ensnare an innocent man, so you too, though you are not a Christian but an Arian, have pretended to be a Christian in order to entangle us. Then, though the Lord's church has always had peace and has cast out you and the heretics of every sect, you said, 'I want peace to be established in my empire'—wanting to violate the Lord's peace among us, desiring to divide the people of God, working on behalf of your heresy, to which you are eager to make us all cross over. So you lied in claiming to be a man of God when you said you were making this peace for the sake of our salvation, just like that false prophet who said: Come back with me, for I too am a prophet of the Lord, and an angel told me. So, I say, you lied when you said that you had undertaken to do this in order to please God, since you were striving to bring the catholic bishops, one by one, into communion with the Arians.

How could Christians have come together with you and your fellow Arians, when you see that God said these things to King Jehoshaphat because he had taken the idolater Ahab into friendship and had gone to war alongside the Lord's enemy? For after that Ahab, your partner in sacrilege, had been struck in battle with a fatal wound, according to the word of God, and Jehoshaphat, because he had cried out to God with his whole heart, had been brought back safe to his house, holy scripture says that Jehu son of Hanani, who was a seer, went out to meet him and said this: If you help that sinner and are a friend of those who hate the Lord, then for this there is wrath upon you from the face of the Lord; yet good words have been found in you, because you removed the groves from the land and prepared your heart to seek the Lord. If these things were said to him, what would be said to us if we had chosen to be friends with you, a heretic and an adversary of God? Or will you dare to say, 'I am not an enemy of God, as Ahab king of Israel was'? How are you not an enemy, when you do the same things Ahab did? For you assail the religion of God just as he assailed it, and you persecute his house just as he persecuted it. How could we agree with you and yours, when that king devoted to God was rebuked by God through a prophet because he had joined in friendship with Ahaziah king of Israel? And Jehoshaphat king of Judah, it says, made friendship with Ahaziah king of Israel; he began to act wickedly, and took him into partnership with himself to build ships to go to Tarshish. And he built the ships in Ezion-geber; and Eliezer son of Ozias, of Mareshah, prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying: Because you made partnership with Ahaziah, the Lord has shattered your work; and your ships were wrecked and could not go to Tarshish. If the Lord says these things to him because he had a king of the way of perdition as his partner in building ships, what could be said to us if we, priests of God, held you—the destroyer of his house, the persecutor of the catholic faith—as a friend? If he shattered that man's work because he had been joined to a wicked man, then we, I believe, would already have been blasted by a thunderbolt for joining ourselves to you, a blasphemer. How could we, who are servants of God, while you are servants of the devil, have come together into one, when God has willed that there be a separation between us and you like that between light and darkness, between life and death, between sweet and bitter; like that between God's holy angels, who are ever magnifying his mercy, and those apostates whom you will see tormented together with you for ever, unless you tear yourself away from them? How, I say, could we servants of God have been with you servants of the antichrist? For God said to King Amaziah in the second book of Chronicles: The army of Israel shall not go with you, for God is not with Israel, with all the sons of Ephraim; for if you think you will prevail with these, the Lord will turn you to flight before your enemies, for strength comes from the Lord. How could we resist the devil if, in so great a crime of yours, we ran along with you in company with the enemies of God, with men found to be without knowledge of God, with those who do not have God, in whom we know there dwells a horde of demons? For you cannot be deniers of the only Son of God without demons, since the only ones who make you blaspheme are those who have blinded your hearts, so that the truth cannot be grasped by you.

Could we really have stayed on your side and consented to your most shameful designs, when the Holy Spirit says through the glorious David that none are blessed except those who have withdrawn from you, the deniers of the only Son of God, and that only those who have not mixed themselves with your serpentine thoughts will remain blessed? Blessed is the man who has not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners, nor sat in the chair of pestilence. How could there be a single meeting place for you and us, when you hear David likewise say in the sixth psalm: Depart from me, you who work iniquity? If you Arians do not work iniquity, judge for yourself, you leader in the sacrilege of the Arians, who persecute us with horrible animosity because we call ourselves Christians. Know, then, that we did right in withdrawing from you, who are hateful to God. For how would it have been fitting for us to remain in your assembly, stained with every crime, and not to flee from you, plagues and pestilence that you are? For he says, speaking in the person of our people, in the twenty-fifth psalm: For your mercy is before my eyes, and I have taken delight in your truth. I have not sat in the council of vanity, nor will I go in with those who do wicked things; I have hated the assembly of evildoers, and I will not sit with the ungodly. If your council is not a council of vanity, prove me wrong. Is that council not vain in which there is no purpose except that the Son of God be denied, that it be maintained that God the Father is not the true Father, that it be asserted that the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, is not the true Spirit of God, that the apostolic and evangelical tradition be destroyed, that the tradition of Arius be established? In that council nothing else is established except what can bring great joy to all heretics and pagans and Jews; all who loathe the religion of God rejoice, because they see you, the emperor, carrying out what they wished for, because they observe that you have become a denier of the only Son of God and a persecutor of his servants. This is the council which you are accustomed to assemble with great zeal and with all the might of your empire, precisely so that all the authority of the sacred scriptures may be dissolved by the authority of your empire, that all truth may be buried, that the lies of your detestable invention may seem to be true. These are your designs in that distinguished council gathered by your power. That is why you hate us: because we loathe your council of evildoers. That is why we are in exile, why we are put to death in prison, why we alone are forbidden to be seen; that is why we are kept shut up in darkness under heavy guard. This is the reason no one is allowed to visit us: because we were unwilling to have any fellowship in your crimes with you, impious and sacrilegious men—you concerning whom a prayer has been addressed to God in our person, that we might not perish together with you by living among you, but might be set apart from your wicked council and from your unjust conspiracy. For he says in the twenty-seventh psalm: Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication, when I pray to you, when I lift up my hands toward your holy temple; do not drag my soul away with sinners, and do not destroy me with those who work iniquity, with those who speak peace to their neighbor while evil is in their hearts. Give to them according to their works and according to the wickedness of their pursuits; according to the work of their hands repay them; render to them their recompense. That is why we are hated by you, Constantius: because we did not want these things to be said of us that are said by the mouth of the prophet about you and yours on account of your wicked work, and that are said about the Jews, whose imitator you have become. Are you not the emperor Constantius, who pretended to be making peace, while your evil thoughts had no aim except that the Son of God be denied, that the apostolic and evangelical faith be destroyed and your Arian heresy built up, that all who would not give in to you be deported, proscribed, tortured in various ways, and finally killed? And therefore the Holy Spirit, marking out and at the same time striking you and yours, says in the person of our people: Do not destroy me with those who work iniquity, with those who speak peace to their neighbor while evil is in their heart. To us you said, 'I want peace to be made,' and in your heart, remaining an adversary of our religion, you were planning to make us idolaters through your agency; therefore you will truly receive according to your work, according to the wickedness of your pursuits, unless you look out for yourself. We have avoided and still avoid your counsel, which has been and is being formed against God; the Holy Spirit, already seeing your designs at that time, spoke of them by the mouth of David in the thirty-second psalm: The Lord scatters the counsels of the nations, and rejects the thoughts of the peoples, and rejects the counsels of princes. God rejects your counsels brought forth against his church; for he cannot hate his people, his inheritance, and love you, children of pestilence, persecutors of his servants.

You said: “Make peace with the bishops of my sect, the Arians, and be at one.” Yet the Spirit of God says through Solomon in Proverbs: “Do not go in the ways of the ungodly, do not follow them, and do not envy the way of the wicked; wherever they have pitched their camp, do not go there. Turn away from it and change your course; for they do not sleep unless they have done evil. Sleep has been taken from them, and they do not sleep. For they feed on the food of ungodliness and are drunk with the wine of iniquity. But the ways of the righteous shine like light; they go forth and give light until the day is established. The ways of the ungodly are dark; they do not know how they stumble.” How could we have fellowship with you Arians, who are spiritual adulterers? We hold fast to what is written: “Do not give heed to a deceitful woman; for honey drips from the lips of a harlot, and for a time it fattens your throat, but in the end you will find it more bitter than gall and sharper than a two-edged sword; and the feet of folly lead those who keep company with her down to the underworld with death.” But what? Do you say these words were spoken about adulteries of the flesh? If you maintain that they were spoken about adulteries of the flesh, how much more must you spiritual adulterers be shunned, so that what is said here may not come upon us through your Arian heresy, that spiritual harlot? To some it seems sweet to be joined in friendship with you, the king, by accepting your heresy. But they will find it more bitter than gall when they begin to be tormented with you forever, when those who chose to be with you begin to feel it in everlasting Gehenna. Then they will say: “Woe to us, who preferred the emperor Constantius to God.” How could there have been agreement between us and you, when Solomon says further on: “Cast pestilence out of the council, and strife will go out with it”; and: “Do not imitate evil men, and do not desire to be with them; for their heart devises falsehoods, and their lips speak mischief”; and: “Do not bring the ungodly near the pasture of the righteous, and do not be led astray by the filling of the belly. For a righteous man falls seven times and rises again, but the ungodly will grow weak in evils”?

How can we be with the proud and the transgressors, with you who have chosen to be found with Judas Iscariot rather than with the most blessed prophets, apostles and martyrs? I hear in the hundredth psalm: “I walked in the innocence of my heart in the midst of your house. I set no evil thing before my eyes; I hated those who commit transgressions; a perverse heart did not cleave to me; the wicked who turned away from me I did not acknowledge; whoever secretly slandered his neighbours, him I pursued; with the man of proud eye and insatiable heart I would not eat.” And in the hundred and eighteenth psalm: “I have hated the wicked and loved your law.” You are wicked, since you deny the only Son of God. We are bound to hate you, because you abandoned the way of truth and seized upon every error, because you abandoned the light and chose to go into the outer darkness. How then could we have been very dear to you, you abominable head, destroyer of the house of God, kindler of all who work iniquity? How could we be your intimate friends, as Valens, Ursacius, Epictetus, Saturninus and the rest are? Even though they see what pit they have fallen into, they would still knowingly choose to perish with you, so long as they may enjoy the empty splendour of your reign together with you. How could we have been with you, when we loathe the very things they have chosen to enjoy with you, and strive to attain the things that will abide forever? Why, then, is there no agreement between us and you? Surely because we refused to accept your heresy, surely because as Christians we refused to become Arians. And who would abandon the house of God and go to the devil's tomb, unless he were out of his mind, as you Arians are?

We suffer your hatred for this reason: we have feared, and still fear, that what was said of those deserters might be said of us. I mean the Jews, whom Jeremiah accuses, saying: “Hear the word of the Lord, house of Jacob and all the house of Israel. Thus says the Lord: What wrong did your fathers find in me, that they withdrew far from me and went after vain things and were brought to nothing? They did not say: Where is the God who delivered us out of the land of Egypt, who led us out and guided us in the wilderness, in an untilled and unknown land, in a land without water and without fruit, in a land through which no man passed and where no son of man dwelt? And he brought you into Carmel, to eat its fruit and its good things; and you came in and defiled the land and made my inheritance a desolation. The priests did not say: Where is the Lord? The elders of my law did not know me, the shepherds acted impiously against me, and the prophets prophesied by Baal and went after useless things.” We did not want to hear these reproaches, and so we declared that you and yours must be shunned. Nor could the members of God's household agree with you foreigners. For we see what God said to that carnal people, your companions in faithlessness: “Turn your foot from the rough road and your throat from thirst. But she said: I will be strong, for she loved strangers and went after them.” So we not only refused to go after you strangers, you foreigners, but we also pronounced anathema on you, sons of pestilence and darkness. We feared that if we withdrew from the apostolic and evangelical faith and abandoned the way held by the most blessed Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, by Abel, Enoch and Noah, and by all the prophets, apostles and martyrs, God would say of us also what was said of your fellow blasphemers the Jews: “As a thief is put to shame when he is caught, so shall the sons of Israel be put to shame, they and their kings and their princes and their priests and their prophets.” We did not want to be among you, so that the rebuke of the divine voice would not also convict us together with the Jews and with you heretics: “Why do you speak to me? You have all acted impiously, and you have all sinned against me, says the Lord.”

How could there have been agreement between us and you? You have read what is written in the first book of Maccabees: “Then a company mighty in strength from Israel gathered to them, all who offered themselves willingly for the law. And all who were fleeing from evils joined them and became a support to them. They formed an army and struck down sinners in their anger and wicked men in their indignation; and the rest fled to the Gentiles to save themselves. And Mattathias and his friends went round and pulled down the altars, and they forcibly circumcised all the uncircumcised boys they found within the borders of Israel. They pursued the sons of pride, and the work prospered in their hands. They rescued the law from the hands of the Gentiles and of kings, and did not give the horn to the sinner.” Could we have been with you, when you see what was done to such men by those who are found to have feared God with their whole heart? You, a limb already cut off from the body of the blessed Church at the moment you became an Arian instead of a Christian, say: “Be with us.” But the Lord says in the Gospel: “If your right eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members should perish than that your whole body should be thrown into Gehenna. And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members should perish than that your whole body should go into Gehenna.” The Church proclaims that she has cut off Arius and thrown him away according to the Lord's commands, and you say: “Take in my fellow plague-carriers and pestilences”; you say: “Let yourselves perish of the same disease of which I have perished.” Sabellius was cut off from the body of the Church just as this Arius was cut off, Arius who is as detestable as you. His teaching has spread in you like a cancer, and so aggressively that you are now seen to be wholly cancer. Nor can you say that the teaching of Arius has not made you cancerous, since the stench of your cancer has reached every place in your realm, and all of us have resolved to avoid you, lest we too be infected by the cancer of your Arian plague. Your master Arius, I say, was cut off and cast away just as Sabellius was cut off and rejected. Sabellius dared to maintain that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are one person, and dared to say that one and the same being is himself Father and Son and Holy Spirit. He was cut off because he did not hesitate to say that the Father himself became flesh in the Virgin's womb and suffered. So Marcion cut himself off and cast himself away, because he refused to confess that the Son of God took manhood from the Virgin's womb and so became man. So Paul of Samosata, the teacher of Photinus, was cut off and thrown out of the body of the Church, because he saw fit to say that the Son of God was a mere man. So too the heretics of every sect have been cut off, just as Arius was cut off, and as you were, who deserved to be cut off because you say of the only Son of God: “He was made out of nothing and is not a true Son; there was a time when he was not.” So all you blasphemers have been cut off and cast out by the power of God from the Church of his mercy, because you did not remain in it in the faith in which the patriarchs, prophets, apostles and martyrs remained. You are a man cut off, together with all your fellow blasphemers, from the body of the holy Church, lying in the devil's cesspit, and you dare to say to her: “Be as I am, so that you may be wasted by the same disease that has consumed me.” So you had supposed that we could come to agreement with you, as if we did not remember that blessed Paul said: “We command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to withdraw from every brother who walks in a disorderly way and not according to the tradition which they received from us.” What reason could have led us to desert the way that leads to the kingdom of heaven and take up yours, which hurls people headlong into Gehenna? You thought you could ensnare us with the cunning by which the serpent ensnared Adam and Eve, drafting an edict in choice words and very fine sentiments, in which all the poisons of your heresy are contained. But how could you have managed that, when blessed Paul has armed us against your poisons and your father's, saying: “This I say, so that no one may deceive you with loftiness of words”; and again: “See that no one deceives you through philosophy and empty seduction according to human tradition, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ; for in him the whole fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily”? How could we have been seduced by those sacrilegious Arian notions of yours, however lofty the words, when we have recognized that what you hold is an empty philosophy? How could your words be sweet to us, when we have seen that you hold to the tradition of Arius and not to that of the blessed apostles? To them the very one whom you deny to be the true Son of God said: “Go, baptize those who believe in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.” How should we Christians desert the apostolic tradition and give in to you, a disciple of Arius? We find you saying that the Father is not a true Father but is only called Father; that he does not have a true Son, but that the Son was made out of nothing; and that the Holy Spirit the Paraclete likewise comes from nothing. We see, on the contrary, that the apostles believed in one God the Father almighty, the true Father, true Father because he truly and not just supposedly has a Son; and in his only Son Jesus Christ, that is, in the true Son of God; and in the Holy Spirit the Paraclete, the true Spirit of God. How could anyone who believes this be tripped up by the devil through you, the founder of the blasphemy of Arius? The apostolic faith confesses a perfect Trinity and acknowledges the one Godhead of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, while the blasphemy of Arius, which is yours, holds nothing except what has pleased your dear devil. The faith of the blessed Church and your heresy are as far apart as light and darkness.

Meanwhile I was right to say that you are separated from us as darkness is separated from light, because you are sons of darkness, and that is why you have vomited darkness out of your viperous hearts. You hoped to turn us aside from the way of truth, as if we did not know that the Holy Spirit had warned us beforehand through blessed Paul, saying: “Let no one convict you, delighting in humility of mind and the worship of angels, who is seen walking without cause, puffed up by the mind of his flesh and not holding fast to the Head, from which the whole body, supplied and joined together, grows to the increase of faith.” How could we follow you, who walk without cause, nursed by the mouth of the serpent Arius, puffed up by the mind of your flesh, an apostate, when the apostle's command compelled us to shun you? You said that for the sake of peace you wished to join the pseudo-bishops of your sect to us. But how could we have done that, and listened not to God but to you, his enemy? We are not senseless as you are, to deny that the Son of God is God, as the Jews deny it, who share your blindness and lead you in your unbelief. Blessed Paul shows the example of their rejection when he says to the Hebrews: “Moses indeed was faithful in all his house as a servant, to testify to what would be spoken; but Christ was faithful as a Son over his house, and we are that house, if only we hold fast to our confidence and the exultation of our hope. Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the provocation, on the day of testing in the wilderness, where your fathers tested me by trial and saw my works for forty years. Therefore that nation became hateful to me, and I said: They always go astray in heart; they have not known my ways; as I swore in my wrath: They shall not enter into my rest. Take care, brothers, that none of you has an evil heart of unbelief and departs from the living God. Instead, encourage one another every day, as long as it is called Today, so that none of you is hardened by the error of sin. For we have become partakers of Christ, if indeed we hold the beginning of our substance firm to the end. While it is said: Today, if you hear my voice, do not harden your hearts as in the provocation. For some heard and did not believe, though not all who came out of Egypt through Moses. And with whom was he displeased for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose corpses lay in the wilderness? And to whom did he swear that they would not enter into his rest, if not to the obstinate? And we see that they could not enter because of unbelief. Let us fear, therefore, that some of you, having forsaken the commandment, may be found unable to enter into his rest. For the good news was announced to us just as it was to them; but the word they heard did not profit them, because it was not mixed with faith in those who heard it. For we who have believed shall enter into his rest, as he said: As I swore in my wrath: They shall not enter into my rest, although his works were finished from the foundation of the world. For he spoke somewhere of the seventh day thus: And God rested on the seventh day from all his works. And in this place again: They shall not enter into my rest. Since, therefore, it remains for others to enter into it, and those to whom it was first preached did not enter because of obstinacy, he again set another day, Today, saying in David after so long a time, as was said before: Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts. For if Joshua had given them rest, he would not have spoken of another day. So there remains a rest for the people of God on a later day. For whoever has entered into his rest has himself also rested from his works, as God did from his.” Who is so foolish that, having read this and received it from the blessed apostle, he would abandon the apostolic faith and try to take up a heresy? Who will dare to deny the one whom he sees has power to grant eternal rest to those who believe in him, and choose instead to believe in the one with whom he will begin to be punished forever? Who is such a man, if not you, the emperor Constantius, who abandoned the Lord's camp and went over to the devil's house? We have not chosen to burn, as you have chosen to burn with your lover the devil; rather, we hasten to enter into everlasting rest. How could we have been caught by your cunning and turned from the way of truth, when the apostle further urges us to lay hold of eternal rest, saying: “Let us hasten, therefore, to enter into that rest, so that no one may fall by following the same example of obstinacy. For the word of God is living and powerful, sharper than any sword, piercing even to the division of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and it searches the mind and the thoughts of the heart. There is no creature that is not manifest before him; all things are naked and open to the eyes of him to whom we must give account”? Since this is so, how could any of us have gone over to you, who persist in the faithlessness of the Jews? What reason could join us Christians to you Arians, when we saw that you imitate that nation in all its faithlessness? How could those who take refuge in the house of God have escaped from that faithlessness, when in the Acts of the Apostles the most blessed Peter spoke thus: “Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For this promise is for you and for your children and for all who are far off, whomever the Lord your God will call.” And with many other words he testified and urged them, saying: “Save yourselves from this crooked generation.” Nor can you say that you Arians are not a crooked generation, as the Jews were and still are. For you see that the scribes, the Pharisees and the rulers of the Jews were then called a crooked generation because they denied the Son of God and persecuted all who believed in his divine majesty. You cannot, I say, claim that you and all the Arians are not a crooked and perverse generation, since you are doing the same things they did. If they denied the only Son of God, so do you; if they persecuted the servants of his eternal mercy, you persecute them too. What, then, should we have done, except withdraw from you sacrilegious men according to the command of blessed Peter? For how could there be agreement with you, when the Lord said in the Gospel: “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy”?

How could we have been one with you? For the blessed apostle, writing to the Corinthians, said: "It is actually reported that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not found even among the Gentiles, that someone has his father's wife. And you are puffed up, and have not rather mourned, so that he who has done this deed might be removed from your midst." If, then, the apostle ordered the man who did such a deed to be removed from their midst, so that the whole church would not be corrupted through fellowship with him, how much more fitting was it that we should flee you blasphemers? If he relates that he handed that man over to Satan, how much more ought you to know that you were already handed over at the moment you began to deny the Son of God? "For I, though absent in body but present in spirit, have already judged, as though present, the man who has done this, in the name of the Lord Jesus, when you and my spirit are gathered together with the power of our Lord Jesus, to hand such a man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ. Your boasting is [not?] good. Do you not know that a little leaven corrupts the whole lump? Purge out the old leaven, so that you may be a new lump, as you are unleavened." Since this is the apostle's rebuke, could Christians be joined to the servants of Antichrist? For how could anyone not have been corrupted by the poisons of your enormous blasphemy, when whoever shares communion with you, whether in pretence or in earnest, is in grave danger? Since because of your heresy we have [withdrawn?] from you, how could we have clung to you again? For the apostle's voice says: "I wrote to you in my letter not to associate with fornicators — not at all meaning the fornicators of this world, or the greedy, or robbers, or idolaters, since then you would have had to leave this world. But now I have written to you not to associate with anyone who is called a brother if he is a fornicator, or greedy, or a worshipper of idols, or a reviler, or a drunkard, or a robber — not even to eat with such a one." If we are commanded not even to eat with you, did you believe that catholics could come together with heretics to celebrate all the sacred rites? Could we be worshippers of God together with you who have wandered off, with you who have been led by the devil's poison into utter drunkenness? How could it have come about that we, the living, should stand among the dead? It was far more fitting that you, the sons of our adversary, should be seen gathered together in one body, and we, the soldiers of Christ, in another, opposed to you, so that you might without any doubt be called by all who love God the members and body of a harlot — a name by which we too could be called if we handed ourselves over to you. "Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them members of a harlot? Far from it! Or do you not know that whoever joins himself to a harlot is one body with her? For the two, it says, shall be one flesh. But whoever joins himself to the Lord is one spirit with him. Flee fornication." What kind of fornication do you think we ought to flee? A man who seeks another woman besides his wife is called a fornicator; likewise a man who serves idols is said to have committed fornication, since he has abandoned God and worshipped idols; and in the same way a heretic is called a fornicator. Judge which of these is the graver crime: to become a heretic, to serve idols, or to commit adultery in the flesh. Since, then, both the Gentiles and you heretics are called idolaters, both parties must necessarily be practising idolatry; and since you will understand that those two crimes are vaster than carnal fornication, more than words can say, see with what evils you have cut your own throat. The most holy apostle cries out still, saying: "Every sin that a man commits is outside the body, but whoever commits fornication sins against his own body," and: "You are not your own; for you were bought with a price. Glorify and carry the Lord in your body." How will you be able to carry God in your body, Constantius, when by rejecting the apostolic faith and embracing the heretical one you have declared that you do not belong to him to whom our fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob declared they belonged, and indeed all the prophets, apostles and martyrs? Further, if the fornicator sins against his own body, how much more do you, who carry out that work of the serpent not only through the flesh but through the soul itself? "Do you not know that whoever joins himself to a harlot is one body with her, but whoever joins himself to the Lord is one spirit with him?" So that we should not ourselves be made one with the sacrilegious in the body of a harlot, and so forfeit being the Lord's servants and become, like you, slaves of the devil, we judged that we had to withdraw from you. Woe to you, who would not be joined to the Lord but chose to be joined to the devil! And when he also says, "Do not be led astray; evil conversations corrupt good morals," what does he bid me do but flee your assembly, stained with sacrilege, so that I do not cling to you and perish along with you?

How could we have taken part in your malignant council? For we find that the blessed apostle said to Timothy: "Do not lay hands hastily on anyone, and do not share in other people's sins. Keep yourself chaste." But how would we be chaste, if by clinging to you we had been torn away, as you have been, from the chastity of the faith by those dearest friends of yours, the unclean spirits? How would we not have shared in other people's sins, since if we had decided to remain with you, we would have become what you are, that is, members of a harlot? How could we be Christians together with you heretics? For we knew that the apostle had also written to Timothy, so that we should draw ourselves away from you heretics: "Teach and urge these things. If anyone teaches otherwise and does not agree with the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and with the teaching that accords with godliness, he is puffed up and knows nothing, but is sick with a craving for controversies and quarrels about words, from which arise envy, strife, blasphemies, suspicions and the evil clashes of men corrupt in mind and bereft of the truth." So it is from you that we have chosen to live apart: from you, who do not believe as the people of God believes; from you, who do not teach as the apostles of Christ, the only Son of God, taught; from you, who do not agree with the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ; from you, the assailant of the teaching that accords with godliness; from you, puffed up against us by our enemy; from you, who know nothing true but are sick with a craving for controversies; from you, through whose wicked efforts quarrels about words, deadly strife and malignant clashes are found to have arisen, especially in our own days; from you, I mean, a man corrupt in mind, a falsifier of the truth. We judged that we must withdraw from you and from your fellow vipers, according to the apostle's precept. For he says further on: "of men corrupt in mind and bereft of the truth, who suppose that godliness is a means of gain; withdraw from such people." How, then, could we have been with you? For in the closing words of this letter he even urges that you must be fled, you who have fallen away from the faith: "O Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you, avoiding profane novelties of words and the contradictions of what is falsely called knowledge, which some have professed and so have fallen away from the faith." We had to avoid you, since you put forward profane novelties of words; for we recognized that you uttered that sacrilegious saying at the devil's prompting — that saying, I mean, in which you expressed the poisons of your doctrine: "There was when he was not," and "He was made from nothing," and "The Father and the Son are not one power." It was not the Holy Spirit who uttered these things through you, but that unclean, devilish spirit. How, then, could we have guarded what was entrusted to us, as the apostle commands, if we had remained with you in your accursed council, when we have resolved to hold the apostolic faith until death — that faith, namely, which we keep as it was written at Nicaea against your blasphemy and against the execrable efforts of all your heretics?

How could we Christians have taken part in your council of Arians? We have heard in the book of Maccabees that our forebears and fellow servants separated themselves from those who had made supplication to idols in obedience to the edict of your fellow tyrant Antiochus: "But Judas Maccabeus, who was the tenth, had withdrawn into the desert, and there he lived with his companions among the wild beasts in the mountains; they stayed there, eating grass for food, so as not to share in the pollution." You see from this one testimony that we had to withdraw from you, so that we too should not share in the pollution. How should we be joined to you? For the Lord likewise says to the apostles: "Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees." And to make clear to us that the leaven was unsound teaching — such as those Pharisees and Sadducees put forward then, and you heretics of every sect put forward now — Scripture continues: "Then they reasoned among themselves, saying, 'It is because we have no bread.' As they reasoned, Jesus said: 'Why are you reasoning among yourselves, you of little faith, because you have no bread? Do you not yet understand, nor remember the five loaves and the five thousand men, and how many baskets you took up, nor the seven loaves and the seven thousand men, and how many hampers you took up? Why do you not understand that I was not speaking of bread when I said, Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees?' Then they understood that he had not told them to beware of leaven, but of the teaching of the Pharisees." Again, since the apostle, writing to the Corinthians, deigns to teach that we must withdraw from you heretics and from all strangers to the faith, how could your heart — fickle and changeable in everything, yet in this malice fixed with great firmness, to the ruin of its own salvation — have presumed that we could be at peace with you or with your people? "Do not take up the yoke with unbelievers. For what partnership has righteousness with iniquity? Or what fellowship has light with darkness? What agreement has Christ with Belial? Or what share has a believer with an unbeliever? What agreement has the temple of God with idols? For you are the temple of the living God; for it is written: I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. Therefore come out from their midst and be separate, says the Lord, and touch nothing unclean; and I will receive you, and I will be a father to you, and you shall be my sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty." Since your precepts are plainly opposed to these promises of the Lord, how could we, the faithful, have remained with you, the unfaithful? Could we who run in the way of light stand with you, men travelling on a road full of the darkness of every error? For who is so foolish that, when he has heard God say, "I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. Therefore come out from their midst and be separate, says the Lord, and touch nothing unclean; and I will receive you, and I will be a father to you, and you shall be my sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty" — who, we say, is so foolish as not to want God to dwell in him, not to want to be counted as received by God among those whom he has deigned to call his sons, and so not to flee you, who have become unclean through your heresy? It did not seem right to us to be together with you, since it is not right for human beings to live among serpents. Or will you deny that in the sacred Scriptures those who deny the only Son of God are called serpents? If you cannot deny it, observe that we acted rightly in fleeing you serpents. You have read the apostle saying to Timothy: "Avoid profane novelties of words; for they will advance far into impiety, and their talk spreads like a cancer." Did you think that men of God could be with you, whose talk is like a cancer? Again, blessed John commands that you be shunned, saying: "I rejoiced greatly to find some of your children walking in the truth, as we received the commandment from the Father. I ask you, lady, not as though I were writing you a new commandment, but the one we have had from the beginning, that we love one another. And this is love, that we walk according to his commandments. This is the commandment, as you have heard from the beginning, that you should walk in it. For many deceivers have gone out into the world who do not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh; these are deceivers and antichrists. Watch out for them, so that you do not lose what you have worked for, but receive a full reward. Everyone who goes astray and does not abide in the teaching of Christ does not have God; but whoever abides in his teaching has both the Father and the Son. If anyone comes to you and does not bring this teaching, do not receive him into your house and do not greet him; for whoever greets him shares in his evil works." How could it have come about that we, together with you and your people, should be soldiers of God alongside the soldiers of Antichrist, when the Holy Spirit, giving these precepts through the blessed apostle, has not even allowed you to be greeted?

But perhaps you will dare to say: "Do I deny that the Son of God came in the flesh, that I should be named one of the antichrists?" You do not, indeed, Emperor Constantius, deny that the Son of God came in the flesh; but you say that he whom we confess to have come in the flesh is a creature, you say that he was made from nothing, and you assert that he is not the true Son of God. We, on the contrary, who hold the tradition of this blessed apostle, believe that he is the true Son of God; we believe that the Father and this his only Son have one deity. That this is so the Lord shows in his holy Gospels, saying: "Whoever has seen me has seen the Father," and "I am in the Father and the Father is in me," and "I and the Father are one." We have often said that, since the Father and the Son are two persons, and yet he says, "I and the Father are one," and "Whoever has seen me has seen the Father," and "I am in the Father and the Father is in me," he wished us to understand nothing other than that the eternity of the Father and the Son is one, their glory one, their power one and their greatness one. It is for this reason, too, that the apostle says in this second letter: "Everyone who goes astray and does not abide in the teaching of Christ does not have God; but whoever abides in his teaching has both the Father and the Son": so that, gathering it from the teaching of the holy Gospels, we should believe in one deity of God the Father and of his only Son, and that whoever believes this has God; but whoever has gone astray from this teaching, that is, "I and the Father are one" — which, being plural, shows both two persons and one power of these two persons, that is, of the Father and the Son — so, I say, the apostle says: "Whoever goes astray and does not abide in the teaching of Christ does not have God; but whoever abides in his teaching has both the Father and the Son," so that we should believe the Son of God when he says, "I and the Father are one," namely, that the deity of the Father and the Son is one. It is clear, then, that you, who do not hold the faith as the Lord handed it down to the apostles and the apostles to the bishops, do not have God; for the apostle too, wishing to make plain the single divinity of the Father and the Son, said: "Whoever goes astray from his teaching does not have God; but whoever abides in his teaching has the Father and the Son." You, I say, who stand without God, who have neither the Son nor the Father — we know that we were entirely right to flee you, since it would not have been fitting for us who have God to stay among the enemies of his divine greatness. But see how hateful you are to God, that we were not even permitted to say "Greetings" to you. How could we Christians be with you Arians? For the apostle Paul says: "Avoid foolish controversies and genealogies and contentions and quarrels about the law; for they are useless and vain. Avoid a heretic after one warning, knowing that such a man is perverted and sins, being condemned by his own judgment." We could not come together with heretics condemned by their own judgment, lest that saying should strike us too, as it strikes blessed Paul's Galatians: "You were running well; who hindered you from obeying the truth?" Knowing you to be enemies of the only Son of God, we flee your wicked counsels, conforming ourselves to the voice of the apostle, who says: "Consent to no one; your persuasion comes from God who calls you. Do you not know that a little leaven corrupts the whole lump?" We, the servants of Christ, refused to receive you, the worms of Arius, into fellowship, so that we should not be consumed by that poison of the devil by which you are consumed. We refused to go along with you — that is, with men who still appear to be outside the knowledge of God, who are still set under the devil's power. We, the living, refused to be joined to the dead, because you are known to be such as we ourselves were before we believed in the only Son of God. That this is so the apostle shows when he writes to the Ephesians: "And you, when you were dead in your trespasses and sins, in which you once walked according to the prince of the power of this air, the spirit that now works in the sons of unbelief — among whom we all also once lived in the lusts of our flesh, doing the will of the flesh and of its designs; and we were by nature children of wrath, like the rest." Since you are still such as the most holy apostle reports we were before we believed, you certainly had to be avoided, men in whom and through whom the princes of the power, the spirits of this air, work and carry out all their desire; you had to be fled, sons of unbelief, by nature children of wrath, so that we should not, by clinging to you, be brought back to what we had been before. We refused to be with you, because you have not yet obtained the mercy of God which we have already received. We refused to have fellowship with you, who were led by the designs of the flesh, as this most blessed Paul was led before he believed — he whom we remember saying: "Let no one deceive you with empty words; for because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of unbelief. Therefore do not become partakers with them. For once you were darkness, but now you are light in the Lord; walk as children of light; for the fruit of light is found in all goodness and righteousness and truth, as you discern what is acceptable to God; and take no part in the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather expose them." Because we have received these commandments, we refused to remain with you and be led by your empty words, so that wrath should not come upon us, as it has come and will come upon you — upon you and your people, upon you sons of unbelief. We refused to become partakers of darkness, since, now believing in the only Son of God and longing to obey the commandments of his majesty, we have escaped from that darkness and become light in the Lord. That is why we have not obeyed your dark commands either: it would have been a crime for children of light to do the work of a man of darkness like you, since the fruit of light is to walk in righteousness and truth and in all goodness.

You say that we act wickedly because we refuse to accept your heresy, and because we have not formed lasting friendships with you and your people. Hear what Moses did about foreigners at the time when God deigned to command him to send a fixed number of Israelites and destroy with the edge of the sword the five kings of Midian and Moab. When the men sent into battle had killed all the males but spared the women who came out to meet them, Moses rebuked the children of Israel for not destroying the women as well. He ordered them to be killed in his presence, declaring that they could entice the minds of the people to worship idols. So if we abhor your heresy as Moses abhorred idolatry, if we long for the heresies of all you who stray to be slain by the sword of God, as Moses wanted those women who were enslaved to idols slain, and if we shun you, the enemies of God's religion, as he shunned the worshippers of idols, then judge that we act rightly in withdrawing ourselves from you. How indeed could we have come together with you, when the apostle said to the Philippians: "Beware of the dogs, beware of the evil workers"? Which of God's servants would not flee from you dogs, you evil workers, unless he had forgotten that he was a Christian? Could we, the servants of Christ, have been joined to you, the enemies of God's religion, when the glorious apostle Jude, the brother of the apostle James, urges us to shun you and those like you and to remain in the faith we have received until the end of our lives? "Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, to those who are called, beloved in God the Father and kept in Jesus Christ. May mercy, peace and love be multiplied to you. Beloved, while I was making every effort to write to you about our common salvation, I beseech you to labour hard for the fellowship that was once for all handed down. For certain men have crept in who were long ago marked out for this judgment, ungodly men, who turn the grace of God into licentiousness and deny him who is our Master and Lord, Jesus Christ." It would have been a crime to come together with you blasphemous deniers, since he goes on to set before us the examples of those who transgressed the Lord's commandments, and so urges our hearts to remain in the faith in which he himself is seen to have remained: "I wish therefore to remind you, though you know all things, that God saved his people out of the land of Egypt, but the second time destroyed those who did not believe. And the angels who did not keep their proper rank but abandoned their dwelling he has kept in chains under darkness for the judgment of the great God [?]. Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them, which in the same way committed adultery and went after the flesh, have been reduced to ashes [?] and set forth as an example, undergoing the punishment of eternal fire. In the same way these dreamers also defile the flesh and despise authority." And further on: "Woe to them, for they have gone the way of Cain, and for gain have poured themselves out into the deception of Balaam, and have perished in the rebellion of Korah. These are blemishes on your love feasts, ruling themselves without fear; waterless clouds carried about by every wind; autumn trees without fruit, dead, torn up by the roots; wild waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; storms that lead astray, for whom a time of darkness has been reserved for ever." And further on: "But you, brothers, remember the words spoken beforehand by the apostles of Jesus Christ, for they said: In the last days there will be scoffers, following their own ungodly desires. These are the ones who cause divisions, worldly people who do not have the Spirit." Because you have been seen to be caught up in all these evils, Constantius, we have shunned your friendship, which labours to destroy us, so that we might not be hurled with you into those places of torment into which, Jude tells us, all those whose path you follow were cast headlong.
